title: Fast-Grasp'D: Dexterous Multi-finger Grasp Generation Through Differentiable Simulation

metadata.authors: Turpin, Dylan; Zhong, Tao; Zhang, Shutong; Zhu, Guanglei; Liu, Jingzhou; Singh, Ritvik; Heiden, Eric; Macklin, Miles; Tsogkas, Stavros; Dickinson, Sven; Garg, Animesh

source_summary: Grasp'D-1M is a large-scale, high-quality dataset of one million multi-finger robotic grasps generated using the fast, differentiable Fast-Grasp'D simulator, enabling more stable and contact-rich grasps and significantly improving vision-based grasping model performance.
abstract: Multi-finger grasping relies on high quality training data, which is hard to obtain: human data is hard to transfer and synthetic data relies on simplifying assumptions that reduce grasp quality. By making grasp simulation differentiable, and contact dynamics amenable to gradient-based optimization, we accelerate the search for high-quality grasps with fewer limiting assumptions. We present Grasp'D-1M: a large-scale dataset for multi-finger robotic grasping, synthesized with Fast- Grasp'D, a novel differentiable grasping simulator. Grasp'D- 1M contains one million training examples for three robotic hands (three, four and five-fingered), each with multimodal visual inputs (RGB+depth+segmentation, available in mono and stereo). Grasp synthesis with Fast-Grasp'D is 10x faster than GraspIt! and 20x faster than the prior Grasp'D differentiable simulator. Generated grasps are more stable and contact-rich than GraspIt! grasps, regardless of the distance threshold used for contact generation. We validate the usefulness of our dataset by retraining an existing vision-based grasping pipeline on Grasp'D-1M, and showing a dramatic increase in model performance, predicting grasps with 30% more contact, a 33% higher epsilon metric, and 35% lower simulated displacement. Additional details at https://dexgrasp.github.io.

We present Grasp'D-1M: a large-scale dataset for multi-finger robotic grasping, synthesized with Fast- Grasp'D, a novel differentiable grasping simulator.
Grasp'D- 1M contains one million training examples for three robotic hands (three, four and five-fingered), each with multimodal visual inputs (RGB+depth+segmentation, available in mono and stereo).

The authors developed Fast-Grasp’D, a differentiable grasping simulator, and Grasp’D-1M, a large-scale dataset synthesized with Fast-Grasp’D, to improve the quality of synthetic grasp data for training robotic grasping systems.

methods.value: The authors developed Fast-Grasp’D, a differentiable grasping simulator, and Grasp’D-1M, a large-scale dataset synthesized with Fast-Grasp’D, to improve the quality of synthetic grasp data for training robotic grasping systems.

problems.value: Generating high-quality, realistic multi-finger robotic grasps for training vision-based robotic grasping systems is challenging due to the limitations of synthetic data generation methods.

hypotheses.value: By making grasp simulation differentiable and optimizing contact dynamics through gradient-based methods, the search for high-quality grasps can be accelerated with fewer limiting assumptions.

evidence.value: The Grasp’D-1M dataset demonstrated improved model performance with 30% more contact, a 33% higher epsilon metric, and 35% lower simulated displacement compared to existing methods.

conclusions.value: Fast-Grasp’D and Grasp’D-1M enable the generation of high-quality, realistic multi-finger robotic grasps that can significantly improve the performance of vision-based robotic grasping systems.
